skills.description: Accumulating a value across loop passes.

CS_RANGE_OFF_BY_ONE.label: Thinks range() includes the end value (one extra pass)
CS_RANGE_OFF_BY_ONE.explanation: Predicts range(1, 5) runs 5 times, or that range(4) ends at 4.

CS_ACC_LAST.label: Thinks a running total only keeps the last value added
CS_ACC_LAST.explanation: Predicts total = total + i ends with just the final i.

hints: range(a, b) starts at a and stops BEFORE b.
range(n) gives 0, 1, ..., n − 1: that is n numbers.
solution: That is 4 numbers, so count is 4.
questions.code:
count = 0
for i in range(1, 5):
    count = count + 1
print(count)

loop_counting.title: How many times a loop runs
loop_counting.big_idea: range(a, b) starts at a and stops just BEFORE b. So range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3, 4: four numbers, not five.
steps: Write out the numbers range gives, starting at the first value.
Stop one before the end value; the end value itself is never used.
range(n) is the same as range(0, n): it runs exactly n times.
Count how many numbers you wrote.
loop_counting.sense_check: The count from range(a, b) is always b − a. range(1, 5): 5 − 1 = 4.

worked_examples.code:
count = 0
for i in range(1, 5):
    count = count + 1
print(count)

loop_accumulator.title: Running totals in loops
loop_accumulator.big_idea: `total = total + i` adds i to what total ALREADY holds. The total builds up each time round, it is not replaced.
steps: Start with total = 0 (or whatever it starts as).
Each pass: new total = old total + the value added.
Keep a trace table: pass number, i, total.
The printed value is the total after the last pass.
loop_accumulator.sense_check: Saving ₹1, then ₹2, then ₹3 in a piggy bank gives ₹6, not ₹3.

worked_examples.code:
total = 0
for i in range(1, 4):
    total = total + i
print(total)

total = 0
for i in range(3):
    total = total + 5
print(total)
